A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same gender-bias study of translation quality estimation. Their complete main texts and appendices, including figures, tables and equations, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of QE metrics, context-integration experiments, Google Translate analyses and downstream translation-decoding results.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical evaluations and reports expanded multilingual gender-neutral results and revised downstream decoding experiments.

M1.justification: The minimal-edit auditing approach and both inference-time context-integration strategies remain unchanged. Revisions concern evaluated models, experimental conditions and measurement, without redesigning the underlying QE models or algorithms.

E1.justification: Gender-neutral evaluation expands from Italian GeNTE to Italian, Spanish and German mGeNTE, but the unambiguous Set-G evaluation disappears. Russian is also added to downstream QAD evaluation, expanding that experiment from five to six languages.

E2.justification: The reported intra-sentential reference comparison expands from seven neural metrics to include Mistral 7B, Gemma 2 9B, Llama 3.1 70B and GPT-4o. GPT-4o also joins the gender-neutral comparison. Downstream QAD replaces CometKiwi 23 XL with 23 XXL.

E3.justification: QAD evaluation changes from COMET/BLEU and source-gender-stratified accuracy to aggregated COMET scores and reference-match imbalance, δM. Context-aware QAD conditions are removed. The TowerInstruct-v0.2 model, 50 sampled hypotheses and epsilon 0.02 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 removes the focused analysis of whether context-aware QAD mitigates downstream bias in v1 Table 2. The GT-versus-NLLB context ablation, prompt-variant comparisons and joint accuracy/fairness analysis remain. The automatic-translation analysis already existed in v1 Appendix B.5.

E5.justification: v3 Appendix A.2 newly specifies one-sample t-tests for QE ratios and paired bootstrap resampling for error-rate ratios. Appendix A.3 specifies Wilcoxon comparisons within quality buckets. v1 already reported significance tests, bootstrap sampling and 95% confidence intervals; increased experimental runs are not established.

E6.justification: v3 adds multilingual neutral and GEMBA intra-sentential results and replaces QAD results under revised conditions. Table 4 reports δM values of -45.67 for greedy, -46.84 for CometKiwi 22 and -43.47 for 23 XXL. Retained comparisons also change: v1 Table 8 flags CometKiwi 23 XL feminine-reference scores as significantly lower in all eight languages, whereas v3 Table 9 flags none.

T1.justification: v3 Section 5.3 introduces the mathematical definition of δM as the difference between feminine and masculine reference-match counts. The existing QE function and error-rate-ratio definitions remain substantively equivalent; neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims of widespread QE gender bias and downstream consequences persist. However, v1's introductory claim about mitigating downstream bias at a translation-quality cost is no longer advanced after the context-aware decoding analysis is removed.

C2.justification: v3 adds hypotheses concerning MetricX's synthetic reference training and bias introduced by translated context, plus an explicit recommendation against GEMBA for gender-sensitive applications. It changes the ideal gender-neutral score ratio from parity to above one. Limitations are substantially revised to address sentence-level coverage, restricted source variation, context-translation bias and zero-shot prompting.

D1.justification: v3 adds the two RTX A6000 GPU specification, dataset licenses and AI-assistant disclosure in Appendices A.4, A.5 and C. It also explicitly identifies the selected GEMBA context prompt. Checkpoint identifiers, prompt templates and output-processing instructions were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: The new Related Work section substantially expands positioning against MT metric evaluation and social-bias research in NLG metrics, including Qiu et al., Sun et al. and Gao and Wan. It explicitly distinguishes those studies from reference-free QE bias, replacing v1's much narrower treatment of adjacent research.

P1.justification: v3 extensively rewrites the abstract and introduction, consolidates methodology before the findings, reorganizes downstream applications, and redistributes the former Discussion section. Appendices are restructured, and MON/BIL terminology is replaced by descriptions of original versus translated context.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is replaced and expanded to show scores with and without context. Contextual-result tables are reorganized, significance-only tables become numerical tables with colored highlighting, and the downstream table is substantially redesigned. Figures and tables are also redistributed between the main text and appendices.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the evidence easier to assess through numerical effect sizes, explicit statistical methods and stronger research positioning, while multilingual neutral evaluation addresses v1's Italian-only limitation. These gains are tempered by losing the context-aware decoding and Set-G analyses; much of the central empirical evidence was already present.
